title: 2021 年全国硕士研究生招生考试 英语（二）

sections.title: Section I　完形填空
sections.dir: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 主线：设定目标会带来意料之外的负面后果。1 题考转折、7 题考因果，2、9 题是副词的语气分寸。

paras.en: It's not difficult to set targets for staff. It is much harder, 1 , to understand their negative consequences. Most work-related behaviors have multiple components. 2 one and the others become distorted.
paras.zh: 为员工设定目标并不难。难得多的是，1，理解这些目标的负面后果。大多数与工作有关的行为都由多个部分组成。2 其中一个，其余的就都会被扭曲。

paras.en: Travel on a London bus and you'll 3 see how this works with drivers. Watch people get on and show their tickets. Are they carefully inspected? Never. Do people get on without paying? Of course! Are there inspectors to 4 that people have paid? Possibly, but very few. And people who run for the bus? They are 5 . How about jumping lights? Buses do so almost as frequently as cyclists.
paras.zh: 坐一趟伦敦的公交车，你很快就会 3 看出这在司机身上如何发生。看人们上车、出示车票。有人仔细查验吗？从来没有。有人不付钱就上车吗？当然有！有检查员来 4 人们是否付过钱吗？可能有，但极少。那些追着公交车跑的人呢？他们被 5。闯红灯呢？公交车这么做几乎和骑自行车的人一样频繁。

paras.en: Why? Because the target is 6 . People complained that buses were late and infrequent. 7 , the number of buses and bus lanes were increased, and drivers were 8 or punished according to the time they took. And drivers hit these targets. But they 9 hit cyclists. If the target was changed to 10 , you would have more inspectors and more sensitive pricing. If the criterion changed to safety, you would get more 11 drivers who obeyed traffic laws. But both these criteria would be at the expense of time.
paras.zh: 为什么？因为目标是 6。人们抱怨公交车晚点、班次稀少。7，公交车和公交车专用道的数量增加了，司机按所花的时间被 8 或被罚。司机们达到了这些目标。但他们 9 撞了骑车的人。如果把目标改成 10，你就会有更多的检查员和更灵活的定价。如果标准改成安全，你就会得到更多遵守交通法规的 11 司机。但这两个标准都要以时间为代价。

paras.en: There is another 12 : people became immensely inventive in hitting targets. Have you 13 that you can leave on a flight an hour late but still arrive on time? Tailwinds? Of course not! Airlines have simply changed the time a 14 is meant to take. A one-hour flight is now billed as a two-hour flight.
paras.zh: 还有另一个 12：人们在达成目标上变得极富创造力。你有没有 13，飞机晚一小时起飞，你仍能准时到达？顺风？当然不是！航空公司只是改掉了一次 14 本应花费的时间。一小时的航程现在被宣传成两小时。

paras.en: The 15 of the story is simple. Most jobs are multidimensional, with multiple criteria. Choose one criterion and you may well 16 others. Everything can be done faster and made cheaper, but there is a 17 . Setting targets can and does have unforeseen negative consequences.
paras.zh: 这个故事的 15 很简单。大多数工作都是多维度的，有多个标准。选定一个标准，你很可能就会 16 其他标准。任何事都能做得更快、更便宜，但这里有 17。设定目标可能而且确实会带来预见不到的负面后果。

paras.en: This is not an argument against target-setting. But it is an argument for exploring consequences first. All good targets should have multiple criteria 18 critical factors such as time, money, quality and customer feedback. The trick is not only to 19 just one or even two dimensions of the objective, but also to understand how to help people better 20 the objective.
paras.zh: 这并不是反对设定目标。它主张的是先探究后果。所有好的目标都应有多个标准，18 时间、金钱、质量和客户反馈等关键因素。诀窍不仅在于 19 目标的一个甚至两个维度，还在于懂得如何帮助人们更好地 20 目标。

items.exp: 定位首段第二句 It is much harder, ___ , to understand their negative consequences。上句 It's not difficult to set targets 与本句 much harder 构成正反对比，插入的副词须表转折，however 符合。therefore 表结果，与"难"不构成因果；moreover 表递进，again 表"再次"，都接不上这层对比。

定位 Most work-related behaviors have multiple components. ___ one and the others become distorted。空格为祈使句动词，"强调其中一个，其余就被扭曲"，正是上句"多要素"的顺承，Emphasize 意为"重视、着重"，与 set targets 时"只盯一项"的动作吻合。Identify 只是"识别出"，不会导致 others become distorted；Assess、Explain 与目标设定语境无关。

定位第二段首句 Travel on a London bus and you'll ___ see how this works with drivers。下文用 Never./Of course!/Possibly, but very few 一连串短答迅速给出例证，说明"一眼就能看出"，quickly see 即"很快明白"。nearly 表程度"几乎"，eagerly 修饰人的急切心情而非 see 的结果，curiously 表"好奇地"，均不合。
定位 Are there inspectors to ___ that people have paid?。检查员的职责是核实乘客是否付钱，check 后接 that 从句表"核查、查明"，与 Possibly, but very few 呼应。claim（声称）、prove（证明）都预设已有证据，recall 是"回忆起自己的事"，主语不能是 inspectors。
定位 And people who run for the bus? They are ___。上句刚说没人查验车票，此处问"追车的人怎么样"，答句应是"没人管、被无视"，ignored 与下文 Buses do so almost as frequently（红灯也没人管）同属"管理缺位"。threatened、mocked、blamed 都需要额外情节支撑，文中无据。

定位 Why? Because the target is ___，紧接 People complained that buses were late and infrequent。抱怨"晚点、班次少"针对的正是准点，punctuality 与 late 构成反义复现，也与下文"按所花时间奖惩司机"一致。hospitality、competition、innovation 都解释不了"晚点"这一投诉。
定位 7 , the number of buses and bus lanes were increased。前句是"人们抱怨晚点和班次少"，后句是"于是增车、增专用道"，两句为因果，So 正确。Yet、Still 表转折（与"整改"方向相反），Besides 表递进，都无法交代"抱怨→措施"的因果链。

定位 drivers were ___ or punished according to the time they took。or 连接两个并列结果，与 punished 相对的只能是"奖励"，rewarded 正确，也与下文 And drivers hit these targets（奖惩见效）相扣。hired、trained、grouped 都无法与 punished 组成"奖惩"这一对照。
定位 But they ___ hit cyclists。上文说司机"命中"准点目标，本句补充他们为抢时间还撞了骑车人，also 表"此外还"，与 But 的转折叠加，凸显"达标却出事故"。only 会削弱撞人的严重性；rather 多与 than 连用表选择；once 表"曾经"，与全段现在时不符。

定位 If the target was changed to ___ , you would have more inspectors and more sensitive pricing。多设检查员、定价更灵活，都围绕"票款收入"，revenue 与 paid、pricing 同属一个语义场。comfort 与"查票"无关；efficiency 太泛；security 已在下一句"标准改成安全"中出现，重复。
定位 you would get more ___ drivers who obeyed traffic laws。定语从句"遵守交通法规"提示司机的特点是"谨慎"，cautious 与 obey 语义一致，也与上句"抢时间"形成对照。friendly、quiet 是性格或音量，diligent 指勤奋，都不能由"守法"推出。
定位 There is another ___ : people became immensely inventive in hitting targets。冒号后是"为达标而挖空心思"的反常现象，属负面，problem 与上段"负面后果"的主线一致。purpose、policy 是中性词，prejudice 指"偏见"，与"另一个问题"的列举逻辑都不合。

定位 Have you ___ that you can leave on a flight an hour late but still arrive on time?。主语是 you（普通乘客），空格要能与 that 从句搭配表"注意到、发觉"，noticed 正确。reported、revealed 侧重"向他人公布、揭露"，admitted 表"承认（错事）"，都不合"个人观察"这一语境。

定位 Airlines have simply changed the time a ___ is meant to take。下句 A one-hour flight is now billed as a two-hour flight 说明改的是整段行程所需时间，trip 与 flight 同义。break（间歇）、departure（起飞时刻）、transfer（中转）只指行程中的某一段或某一时点，与 is meant to take 搭配不通。
定位 The ___ of the story is simple。后文给出"工作多维、选一个标准就会牺牲其他"的教训，moral 意为"寓意、教益"，the moral of the story 是固定搭配。background、style、form 只能交代故事的背景或形式，引不出"道理"。

定位 Choose one criterion and you may well ___ others。上文反复出现 at the expense of、unforeseen negative consequences，说明"选一个就要舍弃其他"，sacrifice 与 at the expense of 同义。interpret（解释）、criticize（批评）、tolerate（容忍）都不含"取舍"之义。
定位 Everything can be done faster and made cheaper, but there is a ___。but 提示转折：更快更便宜，但要"付出代价"，cost 与上句 sacrifice、at the expense of 一脉相承。task、secret、product 都无法承担"负面代价"这一语义。

定位 All good targets should have multiple criteria ___ critical factors such as time, money, quality and customer feedback。空格后列举的是这些标准"所涉及的内容"，relating to 表"与……有关"，作后置说明。leading to 表结果，calling for 表"需要"，accounting for 表"占比例／解释"，都会把"标准"与"因素"变成因果或数量关系。
定位 The trick is not only to ___ just one or even two dimensions of the objective。上文说好目标要有"多个标准"，此处指"只明确一两个维度"不够，specify（具体规定、明确）正确。predict（预测）、restore（恢复）、create（创造）与"维度"搭配均不合逻辑。
定位 help people better ___ the objective。全文讨论如何"达成目标"，achieve the objective 是固定搭配，且与本段"exploring consequences first"呼应。modify（修改目标）与"帮人实现"相反，review、present 也不能与 objective 组成"实现"之义。

sections.title: Text 1　技能再培训该由谁付费
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主线：技能不匹配要靠"再培训"解决，但谁付费难定。22 题问举例目的，别选成"介绍项目特点"。

paras.en: "Reskilling" is something that sounds like a buzzword but is actually a requirement if we plan to have a future where a lot of would-be workers do not get left behind. We know we are moving into a period where the jobs in demand will change rapidly, as will the requirements of the jobs that remain. Research by the World Economic Forum finds that on average 42 per cent of the "core skills" within job roles will change by 2022. That is a very short timeline.
paras.zh: "再培训"听起来像个时髦词，但如果我们希望未来大量潜在劳动力不被落下，它就是一项必要条件。我们知道，我们正进入这样一个时期：所需岗位会迅速变化，留存岗位的要求也会随之变化。世界经济论坛的研究发现，到 2022 年，各职业中平均 42% 的"核心技能"将发生变化。这是一条非常短的时间线。

paras.en: The question of who should pay for reskilling is a thorny one. For individual companies, the temptation is always to let go of workers whose skills are no longer in demand and replace them with those whose skills are. That does not always happen. AT&T is often given as the gold standard of a company who decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy. Other companies including Amazon and Disney had also pledged to create their own plans. When the skills mismatch is in the broader economy though, the focus usually turns to government to handle. Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best, and have given us a situation where we frequently hear of employers begging for workers, even at times and in regions where unemployment is high.
paras.zh: 谁该为再培训买单是个棘手的问题。对单个公司来说，诱惑始终是让技能不再被需要的员工走人，换上有相应技能的人。但情况并不总是如此。美国电话电报公司（AT&T）常被当作"黄金标准"：它选择开展大规模的再培训项目，而不是"先裁后聘"的策略。亚马逊和迪士尼等其他公司也曾承诺制定自己的方案。不过，当技能不匹配出现在更宏观的经济层面时，焦点通常转向政府来处理。加拿大等地的努力说得客气些也只能算迟缓无力，结果造成这样一种局面：即便在高失业率的时期和地区，我们也常听说雇主在求人。

paras.en: With the pandemic, unemployment is very high indeed. In February, at 3.5 per cent and 5.5 per cent respectively, unemployment rates in Canada and the United States were at generational lows and worker shortages were everywhere. As of May, those rates had spiked up to 13.3 per cent and 13.7 per cent, and although many worker shortages had disappeared, not all had done so. In the medical field, to take an obvious example, the pandemic meant that there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel.
paras.zh: 疫情之下，失业率确实很高。二月，加拿大和美国的失业率分别为 3.5% 和 5.5%，处于一代人以来的低点，各地都缺工人。到了五月，这两个数字分别飙升到 13.3% 和 13.7%，尽管许多岗位的用工短缺已经消失，但并非全部如此。举个显而易见的例子，在医疗领域，疫情意味着医生、护士及其他医务人员仍然明显短缺。

paras.en: Of course, it is not like you can take an unemployed waiter and train him to be a doctor in a few weeks, no matter who pays for it. But even if you cannot close that gap, maybe you can close others, and doing so would be to the benefit of all concerned. That seems to be the case in Sweden: When forced to furlough 90 per cent of their cabin staff, Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff. The effort was a collective one and involved other companies as well as a Swedish university.
paras.zh: 当然，无论谁出钱，你都不可能花几周时间把一个失业的服务员培养成医生。但即使填不上这个缺口，也许你能填上别的缺口，这样做对所有相关方都有好处。瑞典似乎就是这种情况：被迫让 90% 的空乘休假后，北欧航空决定启动一个短期再培训项目，让被裁员工转岗去支援医院的工作人员。这一努力是集体性的，还涉及其他公司和一所瑞典大学。

items.stem: Research by the World Economic Forum suggests
opts: an urgent demand for new job skills
a steady growth of job opportunities
items.exp: 定位第一段第三、四句：WEF 发现到 2022 年各职业中平均 42% 的"核心技能"将变化，末句 That is a very short timeline 强调紧迫。B 的 urgent demand for new job skills 正是 core skills will change 与 jobs in demand will change rapidly 的同义概括。A 的 full-time employment、C 的 steady growth 文中未提；D 把"42% 的技能变化"曲解为"关于核心技能的争议"。

items.stem: AT&T is cited to show
opts: an alternative to the fire-and-hire strategy
an immediate need for government support
the importance of staff appraisal standards
items.exp: 定位第二段第三句 AT&T... decided to do a massive reskilling program rather than go with a fire-and-hire strategy。rather than 点明举例是为了说明"再培训"可作"先裁后聘"之外的替代方案，A 正确。B 把下一句"宏观层面才找政府"错接到 AT&T 身上；D 的 characteristics 偏离"作者为何举例"，文中并未介绍该项目的具体特点；C 属无中生有。

items.stem: Efforts to resolve the skills mismatch in Canada
items.exp: 定位第二段末句 Efforts in Canada and elsewhere have been arguably languid at best。languid 意为"迟缓无力"，即力度不够，D 正确；后文"高失业率下雇主仍在求人"正是这个"不够"的结果。A 的 labour costs 文中未提；B 把"成效不彰"偷换成"自相矛盾"；C 的 fierce opposition 无依据。

items.stem: We can learn from Paragraph 3 that there was
items.exp: 定位第三段末句 In the medical field... there were still clear shortages of doctors, nurses and other medical personnel，shortages 与 lack 同义，C 正确。A 的"政策调整呼声"文中没有；B 的 hiring practices 属于第二段企业层面的做法，不在第三段；D 与"失业率飙升"方向相反。

items.stem: Scandinavian Airlines decided to
opts: create job vacancies for the unemployed
prepare their laid-off workers for other jobs
retrain their cabin staff for better services
items.exp: 定位末段 Scandinavian Airlines decided to start up a short retraining program that reskilled the laid-off workers to support hospital staff。reskilled the laid-off workers 即"让被裁员工转做别的岗位"，B 正确。A 的 create job vacancies 是"创造岗位"，与"转岗培训"不同；C 说"为更好服务培训空乘"，方向错（受训的是被裁者，去的是医院）；D 的 college education 无依据。

sections.title: Text 2　英国粮食自给自足的可行性
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主线：脱欧后"粮食自给"听着好，作者用土地与产出一路证伪。27 题分清"报告内容"与"作者设想"。

paras.en: With the global population predicted to hit close to 10 billion by 2050, and forecasts that agricultural production in some regions will need to nearly double to keep pace, food security is increasingly making headlines. In the UK, it has become a big talking point recently too, for a rather particular reason: Brexit.
paras.zh: 预计到 2050 年全球人口将接近 100 亿，且有预测称一些地区的农业产量需接近翻倍才跟得上，粮食安全正日益成为头条话题。在英国，它近来也成了一个热门话题，原因还相当特殊：脱欧。

paras.en: Brexit is seen by some as an opportunity to reverse a recent trend towards the UK importing food. The country produces only about 60 per cent of the food it eats, down from almost three-quarters in the late 1980s. A move back to self-sufficiency, the argument goes, would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation's health. Sounds great—but how feasible is this vision?
paras.zh: 一些人把脱欧视为扭转英国进口食品这一近期趋势的机会。英国生产的粮食只占其食用量的约 60%，而 20 世纪 80 年代末这一比例接近四分之三。按这种看法，回归自给自足将提振农业、政治主权乃至国民健康。听起来很棒——但这个愿景有多可行？

paras.en: According to a report on UK food production from the University of Leeds, UK, 85 per cent of the country's total land area is associated with meat and dairy production. That supplies 80 per cent of what is consumed, so even covering the whole country in livestock farms wouldn't allow us to cover all our meat and dairy needs.
paras.zh: 根据英国利兹大学一份关于英国粮食生产的报告，该国全部土地面积的 85% 与肉类和奶制品生产相关。这提供了所消费食物的 80%，因此即便把全国都变成畜牧场，也无法满足我们对肉类和奶制品的全部需求。

paras.en: There are many caveats to those figures, but they are still grave. To become much more self-sufficient, the UK would need to drastically reduce its consumption of animal foods, and probably also farm more intensively—meaning fewer green fields and more factory-style production.
paras.zh: 这些数字有许多需要保留的地方，但情况依然严峻。要大幅提高自给率，英国需要大幅减少动物性食品的消费，而且很可能要更集约地耕作——这意味着更少的绿地、更多的工厂化生产。

paras.en: But switching to a mainly plant-based diet wouldn't help. There is a good reason why the UK is dominated by animal husbandry: most of its terrain doesn't have the right soil or climate to grow crops on a commercial basis. Just 25 per cent of the country's land is suitable for crop-growing, most of which is already occupied by arable fields. Even if we converted all the suitable land to fields of fruit and veg—which would involve taking out all the nature reserves and removing thousands of people from their homes—we would achieve only a 30 per cent boost in crop production.
paras.zh: 但转向以植物为主的饮食也无济于事。英国以畜牧业为主是有充分理由的：其大部分地形没有合适的土壤或气候来进行商业化种植。全国仅 25% 的土地适合种粮，其中大部分已被耕地占用。即使把所有适宜的土地都改成果蔬田——这将意味着取消所有自然保护区、让成千上万人迁离家园——作物产量也只能提高 30%。

paras.en: Just 23 per cent of the fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK are currently home-grown, so even with the most extreme measures we could meet only 30 per cent of our fresh produce needs. That is before we look for the space to grow the grains, sugars, seeds and oils that provide us with the vast bulk of our current calorie intake.
paras.zh: 目前英国消费的水果和蔬菜中只有 23% 是本国种植的，因此即便采取最极端的措施，我们也只能满足新鲜农产品需求的 30%。这还没算上为种植谷物、糖、种子和油料所需的空间，而它们提供了我们当前绝大部分的热量摄入。

items.stem: Some people argue that food self-sufficiency in the UK would
opts: be hindered by its population growth
become a priority of the government
pose a challenge to its farming industry
items.exp: 定位第二段第三句 A move back to self-sufficiency... would boost the farming industry, political sovereignty and even the nation's health。health 与 well-being 同义，B 正确。A 的 population growth 是首段全球背景，不是"某些人的主张"；C 把"某些人认为"说成"政府优先事项"；D 与 boost the farming industry 正好相反。

items.stem: The report by the University of Leeds shows that in the UK
opts: most land is used for meat and dairy production
more green fields will be converted for farming

sections.title: Text 3　科技巨头的“人才收购”
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主线：巨头小额收购初创，是"买下即杀死"。31 题问事实、33 题问担忧，别把 32 题的态度错记成中立。

paras.en: When Microsoft bought task management app Wunderlist and mobile calendar Sunrise in 2015, it picked two newcomers that were attracting considerable buzz in Silicon Valley. Microsoft's own Office dominates the market for "productivity" software, but the start-ups represented a new wave of technology designed from the ground up for the smartphone world.
paras.zh: 2015 年微软收购任务管理应用 Wunderlist 和移动日历 Sunrise 时，挑中的是两家在硅谷颇受关注的新公司。微软自家的 Office 主导着"生产力"软件市场，但这些初创公司代表了一股从零开始为智能手机世界设计的新技术浪潮。

paras.en: Both apps, however, were later scrapped, after Microsoft said it had used their best features in its own products. Their teams of engineers stayed on, making them two of the many "acqui-hires" that the biggest companies have used to feed their great hunger for tech talent.
paras.zh: 然而两款应用后来都被关停，微软称已把它们最好的功能用在了自己的产品里。它们的工程师团队留了下来，使它们成为众多"人才收购"案例中的两个——大公司借此满足对技术人才的巨大渴求。

paras.en: To Microsoft's critics, the fates of Wunderlist and Sunrise are examples of a remorseless drive by Big Tech to chew up any innovative companies that lie in their path. "They bought the seedlings and closed them down," complained Paul Arnold, a partner at San Francisco-based Switch Ventures, putting an end to businesses that might one day turn into competitors. Microsoft declined to comment.
paras.zh: 在微软的批评者看来，Wunderlist 和 Sunrise 的命运体现了科技巨头无情吞噬路上任何创新公司的冲动。"他们买下幼苗，然后把它们关掉，"旧金山 Switch Ventures 的合伙人保罗·阿诺德（Paul Arnold）抱怨说，这是在终结那些有朝一日可能成为竞争者的企业。微软拒绝置评。

paras.en: Like other start-up investors, Mr. Arnold's own business often depends on selling start-ups to larger tech companies, though he admits to mixed feelings about the result: "I think these things are good for me, if I put my selfish hat on. But are they good for the American economy? I don't know."
paras.zh: 与其他初创投资人一样，阿诺德先生自己的生意常常依赖把初创公司卖给大型科技公司，不过他承认对结果感受复杂："如果自私一点说，我觉得这些对我有好处。但它们对美国经济有好处吗？我不知道。"

paras.en: The US Federal Trade Commission says it wants to find the answer to that question. This week, it asked the five most valuable US tech companies for information about their many small acquisitions over the past decade. Although only a research project at this stage, the request has raised the prospect of regulators wading into early-stage tech markets that until now have been beyond their reach.
paras.zh: 美国联邦贸易委员会表示想找到这个问题的答案。本周，它要求美国市值最高的五家科技公司提供过去十年间众多小额收购的信息。尽管现阶段只是一个研究项目，这一要求却让人预见到监管机构将介入此前一直鞭长莫及的早期科技市场。

paras.en: Given their combined market value of more than $ 5.5 trillion, rifling through such small deals—many of them much less prominent than Wunderlist and Sunrise—might seem beside the point. Between them, the five biggest tech companies have spent an average of only $ 3.4 billion a year on sub- $ 1 billion acquisitions over the past five years—a drop in the ocean compared with their massive financial reserves, and the more than $ 130 billion of venture capital that was invested in the US last year.
paras.zh: 鉴于这五家公司合计市值超过 5.5 万亿美元，细查这些小交易——其中许多远不如 Wunderlist 和 Sunrise 知名——似乎有些离题。过去五年，这五大科技公司平均每年只花 34 亿美元用于 10 亿美元以下的收购——与其巨额资金储备以及去年投入美国的 1300 多亿美元风险资本相比，不过是沧海一粟。

paras.en: However, critics say the big companies use such deals to buy their most threatening potential competitors before their businesses have a chance to gain momentum, in some cases as part of a "buy and kill" tactic to simply close them down.
paras.zh: 然而，批评者说大公司利用这类交易，在最具威胁的潜在竞争者尚未获得发展势头之前就将其买下，有些情况下只是作为"买下即杀死"策略的一部分把它们直接关掉。

items.exp: 定位第二段第二句 Their teams of engineers stayed on，stayed on 即 were retained，A 正确。B 的 market value 出现在第六段，说的是五大巨头，与这两家初创无关；C 把"微软吸收其功能"说成"两家产品功能提升"；D 的 re-priced 文中无据。

items.exp: 定位第三段引语 putting an end to businesses that might one day turn into competitors，以及末段 before their businesses have a chance to gain momentum，说明巨头意在"消灭潜在竞争者"，B 正确。A 把"微软吸收最佳功能"曲解为"夸大产品质量"；C 的 tech talent 来自第二段"求贤若渴"，方向相反；D 无依据。

items.exp: 定位第四段引语 I think these things are good for me... But are they good for the American economy? I don't know。阿诺德承认对自己有利，却怀疑对美国经济不利，C 正确。A 与"巨头更强"相反；B 的 market competition 虽是他批评的内容，但"担忧"的落点在国民经济；D 中他自己正是获益的投资者。

items.exp: 定位第五段 it asked the five most valuable US tech companies for information about their many small acquisitions。FTC 索要的正是"小额收购"的资料，即审查这类收购，C 正确。A 的 limit expansion 属于过度推断；B 把 only a research project（指调查本身）误读为"鼓励合作研究"；D 把"监管早期科技市场"说成"监管初创企业运营"。

opts: set an example for future deals
items.exp: 定位第六段 a drop in the ocean compared with their massive financial reserves：年均仅 34 亿美元，相对 5.5 万亿市值微不足道，说明财务压力很小，A 正确。B 的 management challenges 文中未提；C 的 set an example 与 beside the point 相反；D 的 profits 无依据，本段只谈支出规模。

sections.title: Text 4　直觉有时比深思更准
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主线：深思会干扰判断，直觉在特定情形更准。37 题要抓"想细节"这个因果，别选成"时间限制"。

paras.en: We're fairly good at judging people based on first impressions, thin slices of experience ranging from a glimpse of a photo to five-minute interaction, and deliberation can be not only extraneous but intrusive. In one study of the ability she called "thin slicing," the late psychologist Nalini Ambady asked participants to watch silent 10-second video clips of professors and to rate the instructor's overall effectiveness. Their ratings correlated strongly with students' end-of-semester ratings. Another set of participants had to count backward from 1,000 by nines as they watched the clips, occupying their conscious working memory. Their ratings were just as accurate, demonstrating the intuitive nature of the social processing.
paras.zh: 我们很擅长凭第一印象判断人——这种"经验薄片"从瞥一眼照片到五分钟互动不等——而深思不仅多余，还可能造成干扰。在一项她称之为"薄片撷取"的能力研究中，已故心理学家娜利尼·安巴迪让参与者观看教授们 10 秒的无声视频片段，并给授课者的整体效果打分。他们的评分与学生的期末评教高度相关。另一组参与者在观看片段时必须从 1,000 起以 9 为单位倒数，占用了他们的意识工作记忆。他们的评分同样准确，显示出社会信息处理的直觉特性。

paras.en: Critically, another group was asked to spend a minute writing down reasons for their judgment, before giving the rating. Accuracy dropped dramatically. Ambady suspected that deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues, such as certain gestures or utterances, rather than letting the complex interplay of subtle signals form a holistic impression. She found similar interference when participants watched 15-second clips of pairs of people and judged whether they were strangers, friends, or dating partners.
paras.zh: 关键在于，另一组被要求在给出评分前花一分钟写下判断理由。准确率急剧下降。安巴迪推测，深思使他们把注意力集中在生动却具误导性的线索上，比如某些手势或话语，而不是让细微信号的复杂交织形成整体印象。她发现，当参与者观看 15 秒的两人片段、判断他们是陌生人、朋友还是情侣时，也会受到类似的干扰。

paras.en: Other research shows we're better at detecting deception from thin slices when we rely on intuition instead of reflection. "It's as if you're driving a stick shift," says Judith Hall, a psychologist at Northeastern University, "and if you start thinking about it too much, you can't remember what you're doing. But if you go on automatic pilot, you're fine. Much of our social life is like that."
paras.zh: 其他研究表明，当我们依靠直觉而非反思时，更能从"薄片"中察觉欺骗。"这就像你开手动挡汽车，"东北大学心理学家朱迪思·霍尔说，"如果你开始想得太多，就会忘记自己在做什么。但如果你习惯性地开，就没问题。我们的社交生活大多也是如此。"

paras.en: Thinking too much can also harm our ability to form preferences. College students' ratings of strawberry jams and college courses aligned better with experts' opinions when the students weren't asked to analyze their rationale. And people made car-buying decisions that were both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex—when they had a lot of information to process.
paras.zh: 想得太多也会损害我们形成偏好的能力。当学生不被要求分析自己的理由时，他们对草莓酱和大学课程的评分更接近专家的意见。而当人们被要求关注自己的感受而非细节时，他们做出的购车决定既在客观上更好，也让自己更满意——但仅限决策复杂、需要处理大量信息的情况。

paras.en: Intuition's special powers are unleashed only in certain circumstances. In one study, participants completed a battery of eight tasks, including four that tapped reflective thinking (discerning rules, comprehending vocabulary) and four that tapped intuition and creativity (generating new products or figures of speech). Then they rated the degree to which they had used intuition ("gut feelings," "hunches," "my heart"). Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks, as expected, and helped them on the rest. Sometimes the heart is smarter than the head.
paras.zh: 直觉的特殊能力只在特定情况下才会释放。在一项研究中，参与者完成了一组八项任务，其中四项调用反思性思维（辨别规则、理解词汇），四项调用直觉与创造力（创造新产品或修辞）。随后他们给自己使用直觉的程度打分（"直觉""预感""我的心"）。不出所料，使用直觉损害了他们在前四项任务中的表现，而在其余任务中则有所帮助。有时心比脑更聪明。

items.stem: Nalini Ambady's study deals with
items.exp: 定位第一段：研究名为 thin slicing，内容是让参与者看 10 秒无声视频就给教授打分，结果与期末评教高度相关，说明"第一印象"相当可靠，B 正确。A 的 memory 只是实验中"占用工作记忆"的手段；C 的师生互动只是材料，不是研究主题；D 无依据。

opts: gave the rating in limited time
items.exp: 定位第二段：另一组先花一分钟写下判断理由，Accuracy dropped dramatically；随后安巴迪解释 deliberation focused them on vivid but misleading cues（具体手势、话语），即把注意力放在具体细节上，A 正确。B 把"写理由的一分钟"误当成"评分时限"；C 中 15 秒片段属另一实验，时长并非变量；D 的相互讨论文中没有。

items.exp: 定位第三段引语 if you start thinking about it too much, you can't remember what you're doing。开手动挡的类比说明"过度思考反而干扰本能反应"，A 正确。B 的 memory 只是"忘记怎么做"的表象；C、D 都不是类比要说明的点，deception 只是本段开头的话题。

items.stem: When you are making complex decisions, it is advisable to
items.exp: 定位第四段末句 people made car-buying decisions that were both objectively better and more personally satisfying when asked to focus on their feelings rather than on details, but only if the decision was complex。复杂决策时"跟着感觉走"效果更好，D 正确。A 的 collect enough data 与 rather than on details 相反；B 的 list preferences 属"分析理由"；C 的 expert advice 只在果酱、课程评分处出现。

items.stem: What can we learn from the last paragraph?
items.exp: 定位末段：八项任务分"反思型"（辨规则、理解词汇）与"直觉／创造型"，结果是 Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks... and helped them on the rest，即直觉会干扰反思型任务，B 正确。A 的 takes time 无依据；C 把"理解词汇"归入创造性任务，与括号里的分类相反；D 把"客观思考"与"直觉"的因果说反了。

sections.title: Section II Part B　选小标题
sections.dir: Read the following text and answer the questions by choosing the most suitable subheading from the list A-G for each numbered paragraph (41-45). There are two extra subheadings which you do not need to use. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 先给 A–G 各配一个"动作词"：等、谦、许可、目标、镇静。再读段找同义动作，D、E 是擦边项。
sections.intro: Your boss proposes a new initiative you think won't work. Your senior colleague outlines a project timeline you believe is unrealistic. What do you say when you disagree with someone who has more power than you do? How do you decide whether it's worth speaking up? And if you do, what exactly should you say? Here's how to disagree with someone more powerful than you.

blocks.en: You may decide it's best to hold off on voicing your opinion. Maybe you haven't finished thinking the problem through, or you want to get a clearer sense of what the group thinks. If you think other people are going to disagree, too, you might want to gather your army first. People can contribute experience or information to your thinking—all the things that would make the disagreement stronger or more valid. It's also a good idea to delay the conversation if you are in a meeting or other public space. Discussing the issue in private will make the powerful person feel less threatened.
blocks.zh: 你可能会决定最好先别急着说出自己的意见。也许你还没把问题想透，或者想更清楚地了解群体的看法。如果你认为其他人也会反对，你可能想先召集自己的队伍。人们可以为你的思考贡献经验和信息——这些都会让异议更有力、更站得住脚。如果你身处会议或其他公共场合，推迟谈话也是个好主意。私下讨论问题，会让这位有权势的人少一些威胁感。
blocks.exp: 本段反复出现 hold off on voicing your opinion、delay the conversation、if you are in a meeting，核心是"判断该不该等一等再说"，对应 C Decide whether to wait。D 的 risks 只落在"让对方少些威胁感"，不是"评估风险"；F 的 shared goal 要到下一段才出现。

blocks.en: Before you share your thoughts, think about what the powerful person cares about—it may be the credibility of their team or getting a project done on time. You're more likely to be heard if you can connect your disagreement to a higher purpose. When you do speak up, don't assume the link will be clear. You'll want to state it overtly, contextualizing your statements so that you're seen not as a disagreeable subordinate but as a colleague who's trying to advance a common objective. The discussion will then become more like a chess game than a boxing match.
blocks.zh: 在说出想法之前，先想想这位有权势的人在乎什么——可能是团队的信誉，也可能是按时完成项目。如果你能把异议与更高的目标联系起来，你的话就更可能被听进去。开口时别以为这种联系不言自明。你要把它明确说出来，把陈述放在具体情境中，这样你才不会被视为一个难相处的下属，而是一位努力推进共同目标的同事。讨论也就会更像一盘棋，而不是一场拳击赛。
blocks.exp: 本段关键句 connect your disagreement to a higher purpose 与 advance a common objective，正是 F 的 shared goal 的同义复现。C 已被 41 段用掉；E 的 judgements 与本段"把异议挂到共同目标上"无关。

blocks.en: This step may sound overly deferential, but it's a smart way to give the powerful person psychological safety and control. You can say something like, "I know we seem to be moving toward a first-quarter commitment here. I have reasons to think that won't work. I'd like to lay out my reasoning. Would that be OK?" This gives the person a choice, allowing him to verbally opt in. And, assuming he says yes, it will make you feel more confident about voicing your disagreement.
blocks.zh: 这一步听起来可能过于恭顺，但它是给这位有权势者心理安全感和掌控感的聪明做法。你可以这样说："我知道我们似乎正要在这里做出第一季度的承诺。我有理由认为这行不通。我想把我的理由讲一讲。可以吗？"这给了对方选择权，让他可以口头同意。而且，假设他说可以，这会让你在表达异议时更有信心。
blocks.exp: 本段说这一步给上司"心理安全感与掌控感"，并给出 Would that be OK? 的请求句式，This gives the person a choice, allowing him to verbally opt in，即"先请求许可再表达异议"，对应 G。B 的 humble 属 45 段的语气问题；D 的 risks 无对应句。

blocks.en: You might feel your heart racing or your face turning red, but do whatever you can to remain neutral in both your words and actions. When your body language communicates reluctance or anxiety, it undercuts the message. It sends a mixed message, and your counterpart gets to choose what signals to read. Deep breaths can help, as can speaking more slowly and deliberately. When we feel panicky, we tend to talk louder and faster. Simply slowing the pace and talking in an even tone helps the other person cool down and does the same for you. It also makes you seem confident, even if you aren't.
blocks.zh: 你可能会心跳加速、脸涨得通红，但要尽一切努力在言语和动作上保持中立。当你的肢体语言传达出不情愿或焦虑时，就会削弱你的信息。它发出混杂的信号，对方便可以选择去读哪一种。深呼吸会有帮助，说得更慢、更从容也有帮助。当我们感到惊慌时，往往会说得更大声、更快。放慢语速、用平稳的语调说话，能帮对方冷静下来，也能让你自己冷静。这还会让你显得自信，即使你并不自信。
blocks.exp: 本段从心跳加速、脸红写起，给出的办法是 deep breaths、speaking more slowly and deliberately、talking in an even tone，全是"保持镇静"的具体做法，对应 A Stay calm。E 的 judgements 与"控制情绪"无关；D 的 risks 是判断该不该说，不是控制生理反应。

blocks.en: Emphasize that you're only offering your opinion, not gospel truth. It may be a well-informed, well-researched opinion, but it's still an opinion, so talk tentatively and slightly understate your confidence. Instead of saying: "If we set an end-of-quarter deadline, we will never make it," say, "This is just my opinion, but I don't see how we will make that deadline." Having asserted your opinion (as a position, not as a fact), demonstrate equal curiosity about other views. Remind the person that this is your point of view, and then invite critique. Be open to hearing other opinions.
blocks.zh: 要强调你只是在提供自己的意见，而不是绝对真理。它可能是见多识广、研究充分的意见，但仍然是意见，所以要用试探性的语气说，并稍稍压低自己的把握。不要说："如果我们把截止日期定在季度末，我们绝对完不成。"而要说："这只是我的看法，但我看不出我们怎么能赶上那个截止日期。"在表明自己的意见（作为一种立场，而非事实）之后，要对其他观点表现出同样的好奇。提醒对方这是你的看法，然后邀请批评。要乐于听取别人的意见。
blocks.exp: 本段要求 talk tentatively and slightly understate your confidence，并强调"只是个人意见"、主动邀请批评，即"保持谦逊"，对应 B Stay humble。E 的 Don't make judgements 是"不要评判他人"，与本段"坦陈己见"不是一回事，正是多余项之一（另一个是 D）。

sections.title: Section III　翻译
sections.dir: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 两个长句是难点：while 让步句要把"话虽如此"译出来，due to 后的同位语从句要拆开。

paras.en: We tend to think that friends and family members are our biggest sources of connection, laughter, and warmth. While that may well be true, researchers have also recently found that interacting with strangers actually brings a boost in mood and feelings of belonging that we didn't expect.
paras.zh: 我们往往认为，朋友和家人是我们联结、欢笑与温暖的最大来源。这话也许不假，但研究人员最近还发现，与陌生人互动其实会带来我们意想不到的情绪提升和归属感。

paras.en: In one series of studies, researchers instructed Chicago-area commuters using public transportation to strike up a conversation with someone near them. On average, participants who followed this instruction felt better than those who had been told to stand or sit in silence. The researchers also argued that when we shy away from casual interactions with strangers, it is often due to a misplaced anxiety that they might not want to talk to us. Much of the time, however, this belief is false. As it turns out, many people are actually perfectly willing to talk—and may even be flattered to receive your attention.
paras.zh: 在一系列研究中，研究人员让芝加哥地区乘坐公共交通的通勤者与身旁的人攀谈起来。平均而言，遵照这一指示的参与者比那些被告知默默站着或坐着的人感觉更好。研究者还指出，我们回避与陌生人的随意交流，往往是因为一种错位的焦虑——担心对方并不想跟我们说话。然而多数时候，这种想法是错的。事实证明，许多人其实非常乐意交谈，甚至可能因为得到你的关注而受宠若惊。

words: 错位的焦虑、不必要的担心

sections.title: Section IV Part A　应用文（邀请邮件）
sections.dir: Suppose you are organizing an online meeting. Write an email to Jack, an international student, to 1) invite him to participate, and 2) tell him the details. You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET. Do not use your own name. Use "Li Ming" instead. (10 points)
sections.note: 两个任务点必须都落地：①发出邀请 ②给出时间、平台、主题。只写"欢迎参加"不写细节，第二项不得分。
sections.sample:
Dear Jack,

I am writing to invite you to an online meeting our class is organizing next Friday, and to give you the details.

The meeting will be held on Zoom from 7:00 to 9:00 p.m. on 18 June. Its theme is "Studying in China", and three of our classmates will share their experience of campus life. We would be delighted if you could join us and say a few words about your own first year here, since your perspective would be valuable to us. All you need is a laptop and a stable connection; I will send you the link one day in advance.

Please let me know whether you can come by 15 June.

Yours sincerely,
Li Ming
tips: 开头一句就把"邀请 + 目的"说清，不要写成通知或会议纪要
细节三件套：时间、平台（Zoom）、主题，缺一项就算"tell him the details"没写全
给 Jack 一个具体角色（分享一年级的经历），比空泛的"欢迎参加"更有说服力
结尾要一句回复期限，语气是同学之间的客气，署名固定 Li Ming

sections.title: Section IV Part B　图表作文
sections.dir: Write an essay based on the chart below. In your writing, you should 1) interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. You should write about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 图表：某市居民锻炼方式——独自 54.3%、与朋友 47.7%、与家人 23.9%、团体活动 15.8%。前两项接近是关键。
sections.sample:
The bar chart shows how residents of a certain city prefer to exercise: 54.3 percent work out alone, 47.7 percent with friends, 23.9 percent with family members, and only 15.8 percent take part in group activities.

Two features stand out. First, solitary exercise ranks top, slightly ahead of exercising with friends, which suggests that for most people fitness is a private routine rather than a social occasion. Second, organized group activities come last, even below family workouts, which implies that fixed schedules and formal settings keep many residents away.

In my view, these figures reflect the pace of urban life. Exercise is often squeezed into odd hours, so people choose the form that requires the least coordination. Instead of blaming this individualism, communities could make group activities easier to join—shorter sessions, open-air venues, flexible starting times—and turn exercise into something people look forward to rather than another task to tick off.
tips: 第一段只读数：54.3% 与 47.7% 接近，这一对比是全图最有信息量的地方，别只报最大值
第二段解释"团体活动垫底"：时间难凑、形式太正式，别说成"居民不重视健康"
第三段给一条可操作的建议（缩短时长、户外场地、弹性时间），呼应最低项
注意是百分比，不能写成"增长了 54.3%"；四个数据不必逐一点名
